title: ALLDAY PROJECT Annie: 7 Years as a Trainee, Breaking Prejudice to Achieve Her Dream
excerpt: Moon Seoyun, daughter of Shinsegae Chairman Jung Yoo-kyung. She overcame prejudice that "rich kids have no talent" and family opposition, debuting with THE BLACK LABEL's ALLDAY PROJECT after 7 years of training. Remote lessons across the Pacific, and Melon #1 just 3 days after debut. This is the victory of one who never gave up.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
"A chaebol's daughter becoming an idol?"

In 2018, when a 16-year-old girl knocked on THE BLACK LABEL's audition room door, no one believed she was serious. **Granddaughter of Shinsegae Group Chairman Lee Myung-hee, eldest daughter of Chairman Jung Yoo-kyung**. Why would the heir to a prestigious business empire choose the grueling path of a K-pop trainee? People doubted, mocked, and predicted she would "quit soon."

**Seven years** later. On June 23, 2025, an artist named Annie debuted as a member of ALLDAY PROJECT. Just **3 days later, they topped Melon's TOP 100**. This wasn't a wealthy girl's whim—it was **the victory of someone who never gave up for 7 years**.

## One Music Video Changed Everything

It all started in 2009 with a single music video.

At just 7 years old, Moon Seoyun happened to see **BIGBANG and 2NE1's collaboration song 'Lollipop'** on TV. The dazzling lights, powerful beats, and charismatic performances. **CL's stage presence** in particular captured the young girl's heart instantly.

"I want to stand on that stage."

It wasn't a dream befitting Korea's retail chaebol heiress. Everyone around her naturally expected her to "study business management" and "carry on the family legacy." But from that day she saw the Lollipop video, only **one dream** occupied Moon Seoyun's mind.

To become an idol.

Nine years later, she took her first step toward that dream—**personally** visiting THE BLACK LABEL to audition.

## Family Opposition and the 'College Admission' Condition

"She's lost her mind."

Her family's reaction to the audition acceptance was cold. Her mother's opposition was particularly strong. The heiress to a multi-billion dollar fortune practicing dance and vocals from dawn to night? Jumping into the uncertain entertainment industry? It was an incomprehensible choice.

But Annie didn't back down. Instead, she chose to **negotiate**.

"I'll go to college. I won't give up on my studies. So please let me be a trainee."

This was her **first hurdle**—convincing her family. Eventually, under the condition of 'college admission,' Annie was allowed to begin her trainee life. True to her promise, she enrolled at **Columbia University** in the United States. An Ivy League student and K-pop trainee simultaneously. Two parallel lives had begun.

![A trainee taking video lessons](/images/news/annie-allday-project-7-years-trainee-dream-1.webp)
_Even with the Pacific Ocean between them, training for her dream never stopped_

## Four Years of Remote Lessons Across the Pacific

The time difference between New York and Seoul is **14 hours**.

Balancing K-pop trainee training while studying abroad in America was more grueling than anyone could imagine. Annie received **4 years of remote lessons** in vocals, dance, and rap.

Waking at 5 AM for video lessons with Korean trainers. Attending Columbia classes during the day. Practicing choreography alone in her dorm room at night. This routine continued for 4 years. While friends enjoyed Friday night parties, she was in her small room **practicing precise choreography in front of a mirror**.

"Honestly, there were hundreds of moments I wanted to give up. Every day I thought, 'Do I really have to do this?' or 'Can't I just live an easy life?'"

But she never stopped. The excitement from watching that Lollipop video, the desire to command the stage like CL—these kept her going.

In 2025, Annie finally **took a leave from Columbia** and returned to Korea. She had decided to bet everything on her debut.

## Melon #1 in 3 Days After Debut—Silencing Doubters with Skill

June 23, 2025. ALLDAY PROJECT debuts.

"Chaebol idol," "silver spoon star"—media packaged her with provocative labels. Malicious comments flooded the internet.

*"Didn't she just buy her way in?"*
*"Coming out with no talent, just relying on her background."*
*"Let's see how long she lasts."*

But when the stage began, all doubt turned to **silence**.

Stable live vocals, razor-sharp choreography, captivating expressions that commanded every camera. **Seven years of honed skills** demolished every prejudice. Music critics noted, "Regardless of her chaebol background, her completeness as an idol is impressive."

The results spoke in numbers. Their debut song reached **Melon TOP 100 #1 in just 3 days**, and ALLDAY PROJECT etched their name in K-pop history as the **first official co-ed group in 8 years** since KARD in 2009.

## Youngseo's Story: From ILLIT Dropout to ALLDAY Success

Annie isn't the only remarkable one. Fellow ALLDAY PROJECT member **Youngseo** has an equally inspiring comeback story.

Youngseo was a trainee at Source Music and Belift Lab, appearing on Mnet's survival program 'R U Next?' She ranked 2nd in the final vote—**she was set to debut as an ILLIT member**.

But just before debut, she mutually terminated her contract with Belift Lab. It was the moment her dream crumbled before her eyes. Most people would have been devastated.

Youngseo was different. She immediately applied for **THE BLACK LABEL's audition** and passed. Debuting anew as an ALLDAY PROJECT member, she found **her own place**.

She proved that one failure isn't the end.

## MEARROW's View on THE BLACK LABEL's Training Philosophy

According to MEARROW (K-pop Talent Network) data, THE BLACK LABEL maintains a **top ranking in artist completeness**. The defining characteristic of this label, led by producer Teddy, is **"nurturing that brings out individual colors."**

As seen in Annie and Youngseo's cases, THE BLACK LABEL accepts trainees from **diverse backgrounds**. Whether from a chaebol family or a survival show dropout, what matters is **skill and determination**. A flexible system that allows 7 years of remote training or starting fresh after a pre-debut contract termination.

This is the secret behind ALLDAY PROJECT's immediate success upon debut. **A culture that proves through results**, **a system that offers opportunities without prejudice**—THE BLACK LABEL is showing the direction K-pop industry should head.

## Conclusion: Background Means Nothing Before Your Dreams

What situation are you in right now, reading this?

Are you perhaps thinking of giving up on your dreams because "I don't have connections," "I started too late," or "I already failed once"?

Annie had to fight prejudice **because of** her chaebol background. Contrary to the misconception that "it was easy because she's wealthy," she had to prove herself **more rigorously** than anyone for 7 years. Youngseo overcame the setback of **elimination just before debut** to seize a new opportunity.

In the end, what matters isn't **your background**. Not your origins, not your age, not past failures.

**Not giving up.**
**Getting back up.**
**Going all the way.**

We hope ALLDAY PROJECT Annie's story becomes a small **beacon of hope** for you today.

MEARROW supports everyone chasing their dreams. 🌟
